title: Independent Pronouns
description: Independent personal pronouns are separate words. Their forms identify person and number, and the second and third persons also distinguish gender.

blocks.html: First person refers to the speaker, second person to the addressee, and third person to someone or something being discussed. First-person pronouns are common gender; second- and third-person forms distinguish masculine and feminine. Hebrew verbs often mark the subject themselves, so an independent pronoun can add emphasis or contrast.

didYouKnow: According to OSHB/MorphHB (CC BY 4.0), the most frequent word in this unit is הוּא (hû’), occurring 1592 times in the Westminster Leningrad Codex.
